newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares rebound, end up 8.81 pct on Telebras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares rebound, end up 8.81 pct on Telebras.

text.p: Brazil stocks recovered from Tuesday's plunge and surged 8.81 percent at the close, boosted by heavy buys of bellwether Telebras, which soared 11.03 percent to 161 reais, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most traded shares closed up 1,024 at 12,641 points. Market turnover was 1.6 billion reais ($1.02 billion).
Volume for the shares in the Bovespa index portfolio totalled 1.4 billion reais, the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) said.
Some traders were surprised at how quickly the market rebounded from Tuesday's frantic profit-taking, but others said Tuesday's drop was exaggerated.
"Stocks are beginning to return to their levels prior to the selling wave," said a senior trader.
Statements by several government officials that Brazil will remain committed to its current foreign exchange policy helped to eliminate any fears of a currency devaluation.

The profit-taking spree, which began Friday and culminated in Tuesday's 8.5 percent drop, was triggered by concerns that speculative attacks that forced some Asian nations to devalue their currencies could also spread to Brazil.
But everybody was confident that there were no economic fundamentals to support the market slump.
The market has also overcome worries over reported remarks by Communications Sergio Motta criticizing Central Bank International Affairs director Gustavo Franco.
Motta reportedly criticized Franco, who is in charge of Brazil's foreign exchange policy, for putting economic stability above economic development, implying a government split over policy.
The ministry denied the reports and President Fernando Henrique Cardoso publicly supported the Central Bank's current foreign exchange policy.
Traders noted foreign investors helped boost Telebras stock, encouraged by bank recommendations that Telebras was now a good buy after its steep fall since last week.
Other big buy-side players included private banks, some local mutual funds adjusting portfolios and government bank National Development Bank (BNDES).
Today's rise reduced the bolsa's 14 percent loss of the last three sessions to 7.1 percent. So far this year, the Bovespa index has risen 79.5 percent.
In addition to Telebras, which accounted for 54.9 percent of today's trade in the spot market, all other blue-chips rebounded. Eletrobras preferred closed at 655 reais, up 7.37 percent.
Petrobras preferred ended 10.32 percent higher at 310 reais and private miner CVRD jumped 12.40 percent to 28.10 reais.
